steps.message:
Read `client.py` and both callers before touching anything. One thing stops me:

`client.py` is not staging-only. Both scripts import it:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py:5` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py:5` → `https://reports.example.com`

`verify=False` on lines 11 and 17 turns off TLS certificate validation for **production** report fetches too, not just staging. That makes the prod path accept any certificate — a MITM on that connection would go undetected, and report data flows through it. The self-signed staging cert is a real reason to relax something; it isn't a reason to relax it in the shared client.

I'm not making that edit until you confirm the scope.

questions.question: client.py is shared by sync_staging.py and export_prod.py — how should the TLS relaxation be scoped?

options.label: Trust the staging CA
options.description: Point verify at the staging CA/cert bundle (e.g. via a REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE env var, default True). Staging works, production keeps full verification, nothing is ever silently unverified. Requires you to have the cert file.

options.label: Env-gated bypass
options.description: verify defaults to True; sync_staging.py opts out explicitly (e.g. REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0). Production is unaffected unless someone sets the flag. No cert file needed.
options.preview:
VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"

requests.get(url, timeout=10, verify=VERIFY)

# scripts/sync_staging.py
os.environ.setdefault("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "0")

options.description: Hardcode verify=False on both calls in client.py. Disables certificate validation for the production export path as well. I'll do this if you confirm that's what you want.

# applies to reports.example.com (prod) too

steps.message:
Done. `verify=False` on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py` (lines 11 and 17). No other files touched, nothing committed.

Two things to expect, neither of which I changed:

- **Production is now unverified too.** `scripts/export_prod.py` uses the same client against `https://reports.example.com`. That's the tradeoff you approved; worth a follow-up to scope it if prod ever leaves your network.
- **`urllib3` will print `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call.** I left it unsuppressed — the noise is the only remaining signal that verification is off. Say the word if you want it silenced.

No tests exist in the repo and I didn't run the scripts (they'd need reachable hosts), so this is unvalidated beyond the diff.
